## Sculpted owl feathers in Windows 0.24.30

Owl sculptures now have overlapping rows of feather relief across their wings and back. Each vane has a tapered tip and a central ridge. The surface extends farther along the folded wings and transitions back to the underlying shape towards the face, crown and feet. The relief is part of the exported mesh. Its highlights move with the viewing angle and the feathers remain visible with the textures disabled.

The studio applies the shape pass before rendering the side references and reduces the repeated paint pattern over the sculpted areas. Both reconstruction engines use the same relief. The pass targets upright owl sculptures and skips featherless prompts and common descriptions of an owl printed on another object.

## Painted and unpainted owl comparison, Windows 0.24.30

Applied the geometry pass to the exact 146,912-triangle owl from 0.24.29. Rendered matched side and back views under the same light with every color texture disabled. Layered vanes are visible on both wings and the rear mantle. Compared the exports and verified unchanged triangle connectivity, front-reference positions, UV coordinates and all embedded image pixels. The maximum displacement was 1.93% of the normalized model height and no triangle reversed its orientation. Also checked unrelated subjects, an owl depicted on a mug and a featherless owl against the subject filter.

A fresh prompt in the packaged Windows app on the RTX 3060 produced a 5,611,320-byte owl with 147,799 triangles in 193.0 seconds. Verified that its saved receipt includes feather relief, the GLB contains four embedded textures, the model rotates through all four views, and the exported fingerprint matches the saved model.
